proof_review: K is the index-two subgroup of F13 multiplicative units, contains -1, and excludes 2. Determinant incidence is well defined. SL2 is transitive on ordered adjacent pairs and its decorated action has kernel plus/minus I.

Scalar 2 is a commuting involution on decorations and is outside PSL2. The resulting group has order 2184. Distinct projective lines admit a common neighbour by two independent determinant equations; antipodes have none. Thus an automorphism fixing a vertex and all its neighbours fixes the entire graph.

The local graph is Paley13. Its six neighbours of zero form the displayed cycle. The six distinct attachment triples form one rotation orbit but exclude its reflected orbit. The local point stabilizer therefore has size at most six, giving the full graph automorphism bound 28*13*6=2184.

The full group is free on ordered triangles and their count is 2184, hence transitive. Solving a and 1-a in K gives precisely 4 and 10, so every triangle has two completions. Every actual flag extends and every panel has two chambers.

Different graph vertices have different neighbourhoods. For any two types, a third type compares their neighbourhood images, forcing all type permutations to coincide. Therefore the full type-preserving group is exactly the diagonal graph automorphism group, rather than an assumed subgroup. Its two chamber orbits alternate at every panel.
The actual residue at types1,2 is the bipartite double of the even six-cycle, hence two disconnected six-cycles. It is the incidence residue, not merely an internal coset subgeometry.

All six difference elements have projective order three and fix the specified two decorations. Two distinct complements of order three in C13:C3 generate the whole point stabilizer. Upper and lower translations generate PSL2. Triple stabilizers are trivial, so these stabilizer identities prove all subset intersections and generator independence.

The source uses right cosets H_i*g. Mapping these to g^-1*v_i has exactly the stated fibres. Ordered-edge transitivity identifies all six coset incidence relations with determinant incidence. Thus the marking satisfies Construction3.2 literally.

The source definition of chirality uses the full type-preserving automorphism group, with no assertion that it equals the specified C-plus group. The printed496 passage incorrectly transfers proper-flag transitivity from that full group to the specified group. This example has index two and refutes the stated Theorem1.1.
